rules.statement: Do not use InternalsVisibleTo to let one production assembly access another production assembly's internal types; make packages collaborate through deliberately designed public contracts instead.
rules.why: Cross-assembly internals access creates hidden coupling that consumers can't see and PublicApiAnalyzers doesn't track, so a refactor that is safe inside one assembly can quietly break another.
rules.check: Look for InternalsVisibleTo attributes or <InternalsVisibleTo> items in csproj/AssemblyInfo whose target is a non-test production assembly.

rules.statement: Grant InternalsVisibleTo only to the matching *.Tests assembly and to DynamicProxyGenAssembly2 (so Moq/Castle can proxy internal types and internal virtual members).
rules.why: Test projects and mocking proxies are the only consumers allowed to see internals; any other target turns the package boundary into an invisible dependency.
rules.check: Every InternalsVisibleTo target must be the assembly's own *.Tests project or DynamicProxyGenAssembly2; flag any other target.

rules.statement: Mark a type or member that is public only for cross-assembly infrastructure collaboration, and not meant for application code, with [EditorBrowsable(EditorBrowsableState.Never)], and start its <summary> with the standard sentence "This API supports the ... infrastructure and is not intended to be used directly from your code."
rules.why: This follows the EF Core / ASP.NET Core pattern: the collaboration surface stays explicit and version-tracked, but it doesn't show up in application developers' IntelliSense.
rules.check: A new public type or member that exists only for use by sibling packages but lacks [EditorBrowsable(EditorBrowsableState.Never)] or the standard infrastructure sentence at the start of its <summary>.
